sentences.text: Before we read anyone else’s lights, we need the vocabulary, and that’s Rule twenty-one.
Look at the diagram as I go around the boat.
The masthead light is white, on the centerline, and it shines over two hundred twenty-five degrees: from dead ahead to twenty-two and a half degrees abaft the beam on each side.
The sidelights are green to starboard and red to port.
Each one covers one hundred twelve and a half degrees, from dead ahead to twenty-two and a half degrees abaft the beam on its own side.
On a vessel under twenty meters, they can be combined in one lantern.
The sternlight is white, and it covers the remaining one hundred thirty-five degrees aft.
Two sidelights make two hundred twenty-five degrees, the same as the masthead light.
Add the sternlight’s one hundred thirty-five, and you have the full circle, three hundred sixty.
That’s why you see either her sidelights or her sternlight, never both.
A towing light is yellow, with the same arc as a sternlight.
An all-round light shows through the full three hundred sixty degrees.
And a flashing light flashes one hundred twenty times a minute or more.
